title: SQL & persistent data
theory: A relational table holds rows with named columns. A primary key identifies a row; a foreign key relates it to another table. Choose constraints to represent actual rules rather than relying only on form validation.
WHERE filters input rows. GROUP BY defines groups and aggregate functions summarize them. HAVING filters groups. ORDER BY makes output ordering explicit; without it, do not assume the display order.
A join combines related rows. An inner join excludes unmatched rows. A left join preserves left-side rows, but COUNT(*) and COUNT(right.id) can produce different answers for unmatched records.

Every automatic SQL task runs one SELECT against a fresh, synthetic SQLite fixture. Use the displayed schema and row contracts. The downloadable checker tests multiple fixtures; results are arrays of rows, in the requested order.

quiz.explanation: WHERE applies to input rows; HAVING applies to groups.

quiz.explanation: NULL needs IS NULL rather than ordinary equality.

quiz.explanation: A left join keeps every left-side row, even without a match.

tasks.title: Repair grouped totals
tasks.brief: Repair the query that tries to filter aggregate values in WHERE.
requirements: Keep only categories with total power >=80.
tasks.starter:
SELECT category, SUM(quantity * watts) AS total
FROM equipment
WHERE SUM(quantity * watts) >= 80
GROUP BY category
ORDER BY category;
